exchange.rackcraft.footer_all: Almost every survival item is for sale. Scroll to browse; dimmed items are beyond your balance.

generator.rackcraft.no_fuel: No fuel: add coal, coke or biodiesel
guide.rackcraft.chapter.advanced_chips.i: Past the Wafer-Scale Engine, hardware is manufactured, not crafted or bought. Four research projects open it up. Advanced Materials (after Cryogenic Hydrogen Storage) unlocks two new processing cubes, the CVD Furnace for Graphene and the Epitaxy Reactor for Gallium Nitride, both hungry for hydrogen, and Superconducting Wire on the Assembly Line. Chiplets and Advanced Packaging (after Extreme UV Lithography) lets an Assembly Line dice a Wafer-Scale Engine into eight chiplets. That is the silicon lottery: the whole wafer bins as one, 60% bronze, 30% silver and only 10% gold, and better modules need better bins. Silicon Photonics turns Gallium Nitride and silver chiplets into Photonic Interconnects. None of these materials or chips is sold on the Crypto Exchange.
guide.rackcraft.chapter.advanced_racks.i: Three bigger racks, each built on the Assembly Line from the one below and each behind its own research. The High-Density Rack has 12 bays and a built-in rear-door cooler. The Liquid-Immersion Rack has 16 bays and puts all its heat into the coolant loop. The Exascale Cabinet has 24 bays, runs everything 20% faster on half the fiber bandwidth, and only takes tier 2 hardware and up. New modules all start as a Blade Chassis; the first part fitted decides what it becomes. Quantum Annealers mine twice what a Quantum Core does but need a Cryostat beside their rack, fed with hydrogen. NPUs serve contracts and leases only, and FPGAs can be reflashed between jobs.
guide.rackcraft.chapter.ai.intro: Racks can do more than mine. Clients post contracts at the Operations Terminal: an image of something absurd, or an essay, a legal document, somebody's homework. Accept one, press Generate and pick a cluster (it needs an uplink router), and its racks work until the item reaches the required quality; finished work lands in the outbox and is delivered automatically. Pay beats mining on the same racks, more so with Tensor Accelerators, and late work earns half. Each kind of work has a lineup of models, like a real lab's: Lite models are fast and learn from a few examples but top out early, Pro models are slow and data-hungry but end up far better, and Flash sits between. Pick one per contract, or leave it on Auto for the fastest that reaches the quality. Every model trains separately, on training data: children drawing at a Kids' Art Table, and librarians shackled to Scriptorium Desks. Upload what they make to a model at the terminal and idle racks train it. Keep spare finished work: clients often order the same thing again.
guide.rackcraft.chapter.components.intro: Every module and machine is built from the same few components. Circuit boards come first, then CPUs, RAM and GPUs.
guide.rackcraft.chapter.compute.intro: A rack has eight bays, one module each. Earnings need power of at least 50% satisfaction, a fiber link to a router, and a cool intake. Above 27 C performance falls, and at 40 C the rack stops. A rack whose power drops below 50% trips and stays off until its inlet is under 32 C. The biggest module of all, the Wafer-Scale Engine, comes from a Wafer Fab once you've researched it: see R&D and the Frontier. Bigger racks, with 12 to 24 bays, come later: see Advanced Racks and Modules.
guide.rackcraft.chapter.construction.int: Placing a hundred Solar Arrays by hand is a job for drones. Mark out a site with a Survey Stake, hand it to a Site Planner on your grid, choose a Solar Field, a Tracking Solar Field, a Wind Farm or a Data Hall, and press Start. The work always goes in the same order: Construction Drones clear everything soft off the site, Terraforming Drones level it (five blocks a trip) and dock once it is even, then Construction Drones build the layout and wire it back to the planner. Materials, drones and hydrogen come from the planner's slots or from storage on its Item Pipe, and its screen says what it is waiting for. A Storage Exporter beside it can stock it from storage instead, and with Buy switched on it pays for cable and fill earth at the Crypto Exchange. Arrays, tower parts and drones always come from your own Assembly Line. With Docks switched on, a fifth phase places and stocks Drone Docks to service the finished site. A Data Hall is the densest, coolest rack layout there is, bought on the company card: columns of four Quantum Core racks in two tiers, back to back on CDUs that catch all their exhaust, with cold aisles between row pairs, Core Routers and Chillers on top, and no cables at all. Each column mines 1,920 RC/s on about 360 kW, so check the planner's power estimate against your grid first.
guide.rackcraft.chapter.cooling.intro: Every kilowatt a rack draws comes back out as heat, and a rack slows down once its intake air passes 27 C and stops at 40 C. Heat leaves a rack two ways. AIR: out of the back into the room, where it spreads and slowly leaks through the walls (outdoors it blows away much faster). Keep it off the intakes with hot and cold aisles, blanking panels and raised floor, or catch it with a Rear-Door Cooler, a CRAC unit or an exhaust fan. LOOP: liquid-cooled modules (ASIC and up) send 85% of their heat down a Coolant Pipe, and Rear-Door Coolers, CRACs and reactors put heat into the same pipes. Every pipe network is one loop, and heat sinks on it take the heat out: Cooling Towers (with water from a Freshwater Pump), Dry Coolers, Chillers and Water Heat Exchangers. A loop can only take what its sinks can; any extra stays in the air. Open a rack to see how much of its heat goes to the loop and how much to the air, and check a loop with the Multimeter.
guide.rackcraft.chapter.creative.intro: Creative-only machines for building and testing. They cannot be crafted or bought at the Exchange; find them in the Rackcraft Creative tab. Right-click one to set its value in-game; only players in creative mode or operators can change it.
guide.rackcraft.chapter.fuels.intro: Diesel generators are your insurance against outages, and they need fuel. Rackcraft fuels also work in vanilla furnaces.
Rackcraft is about running a data centre. Racks of servers mine RackCoin, but every kilowatt they draw comes back out as heat. Mine bauxite, smelt aluminium, blast iron into steel and quartz into silicon, then build up to your first rack. Keep an eye out for abandoned data centers on the surface: fix their cut cables and they start mining for you.
guide.rackcraft.chapter.industry.intro: Once RackCoin stops mattering, power is what's left to spend. The Electrolyser turns hundreds of megawatts into hydrogen: Hydrogen Canisters, or with a Hydrogen Tank on its network, gas piped straight into the tank (no ingots needed), which storage then hands out as canisters. An Exchange Auto-Buyer on a storage network buys whatever its machines run short of, and the Assembly Line turns parts into machines no crafting table can make: lay Conveyor Belts past a row of robot arms (Welding, Riveting and Assembly Robots, each facing the belt) and each arm does its step as a workpiece passes. A Drone Frame goes in one end and a Maintenance Drone comes out the other. Belt Loaders feed a line from storage and Belt Unloaders file what comes off it, and a Storage Exporter keeps any machine or chest beside it stocked from storage. Drones live in a Drone Dock and fix failed modules (always with the same kind), cut cables and tripped breakers by themselves, and service worn Solar Arrays and Wind Towers; on an Item Pipe the dock restocks itself from storage.
guide.rackcraft.chapter.mining.intro: Power -> racks -> RackCoin -> Crypto Exchange. Fill a Server Rack with modules, power it with Power Cable, link it to an Uplink Router with Fiber Cable, and keep its front intake below 27 C. Working racks mine RackCoin every second into one shared balance. Open a rack to see its rate or what is wrong, then spend the coin at a Crypto Exchange, or bid it on rarer things at a Darknet Terminal. The Exchange sells nearly everything, but Rackcraft hardware carries a steep premium (components four times, machines six times their value), so building your own stays the cheaper way to grow.
guide.rackcraft.chapter.movement.intro: A campus is a long walk. A Grapple gets you onto a roof, a Hydrogen Jetpack gets you over it and lets you hover, a Mag-Lev line runs a car between stations, and Quantum Teleport Pads skip the trip entirely for power and a little hydrogen. Personal Propulsion, Magnetic Levitation and Quantum Entanglement in the R&D tab unlock them.
guide.rackcraft.chapter.nuclear.intro: The full fuel cycle, and every machine in it is a multiblock: a solid cube of the same machine, 2x2x2 up to 5x5x5 (or 10x10x10 with research), and a serious power draw. Mine Uranium Ore deep underground; a Uranium Mill turns two Raw Uranium into a Yellowcake; a Gas Centrifuge enriches six Yellowcake into one Enriched Uranium and four Depleted Uranium; a Fuel Fabricator makes one Fuel Cell from each Enriched Uranium and two Steel Ingots; Modular Reactors burn them and leave Spent Fuel, which stops the reactor once its waste slots fill up. Spent Fuel is radioactive in your pockets: a Cask Sealer seals four of them with four Depleted Uranium into a harmless Waste Cask. Each cube's products gather in its port, the bottom corner framed in cyan: open it and press Collect all. A cube short of power runs slower rather than stopping. Connect every cube to a Storage Array with Item Pipe and the whole cycle runs by itself.
guide.rackcraft.chapter.operations.intro: Connect racks over fiber to routers to sell compute. The Facility Controller tracks RackCoin and availability, runs a small parts shop, and warns you of events. They are real: a utility outage cuts Utility Intakes; a cooling failure stops every sink; a heat wave makes intakes 4 C hotter and costs dry coolers and towers 30%; a hardware failure burns one module per 64 racks into a Failed Module (never a Quantum Core or Wafer-Scale Engine, and never once Predictive Maintenance is researched); a cable cut cuts a cable; and a surge reboots every rack on a power network with no battery on it.
guide.rackcraft.chapter.power.intro: Every machine touching the same Power Cable run, or touching another power machine, is on one network. Each network draws on its sources in a fixed order: power beamed down from orbit first, then solar, wind, reactors and the utility feed, then batteries, then diesel. Surplus charges batteries. When power runs short, cooling and other machines are fed before racks. Battery Banks built into a solid cube (2x2x2 up to 5x5x5, or 10x10x10 with research) become one Grid-Scale Battery, bigger and less lossy per bank. The bigger Solar Arrays and Wind Towers come off the Assembly Line: see Wind and Solar at Scale.
guide.rackcraft.chapter.renewables.intro: The Assembly Line tier of renewables. A Solar Array is six panels on one 3x2 frame (36 kW, and arrays that touch share power without cables); a Tracking Solar Array makes 47 kW and keeps going at 60% through dawn and dusk. A Wind Tower is a nacelle on at least ten Tower Sections with a clear 5x5 in front for its blades: 120 kW at Y 130, up to 150 kW higher up. One wind blows for the whole world and rises and falls over a few minutes, so batteries smooth it out. These machines wear, losing up to 30% over three days of running, until a Maintenance Drone services them; the basic panel and turbine never wear. A Site Planner can build whole fields of them.
guide.rackcraft.chapter.rnd.intro: Once the cluster is big, the Operations Terminal's R&D tab turns its spare compute and RackCoin into upgrades. Every project costs RackCoin to start and then compute-seconds, which idle racks on Auto clusters work through instead of mining: General projects use general compute, AI projects use AI compute, and the Research share button decides how much of the free compute research may take. Projects come in tiers (faster boots, cheaper power, better sinks, cheaper training, a wider thermal envelope, reactor uprates, and Extreme UV Lithography, which unlocks the Wafer Fab). Repeatables never end: each level costs 2.5 times the RackCoin and twice the compute. Enterprise Sales unlocks Compute Leases: clients rent a share of your AI compute for up to an hour with a 99% or 99.9% uptime guarantee, paying in full only if you keep it (5% less for every 0.1% short). Offers grow with your facility. Frontier runs train ever bigger models on your single biggest Auto cluster, which must keep lending the run's minimum AI compute the whole time: if it drops (an outage, a trip, an overheated hall) the run rolls back to its last checkpoint, every 5%. Pause a run before maintenance and it saves a checkpoint where it stands. The fifth run is an AGI.
guide.rackcraft.chapter.space.intro: Hydrogen's real job. Build Rocket Stages and payloads on the Assembly Line, fill a Launch Control's tank with Hydrogen Canisters, and put things in orbit. Comms Satellites speed up the Darknet and add lease slots, Survey Satellites find a Hyperscale Campus for you, Orbital Data Centers add compute to every rack, and Dyson Mirrors beam power back down to Rectennas. The last two have no limit.
guide.rackcraft.chapter.storage.intro: Store items on drives in Storage Arrays, cold-archive them on tape, and reach it all from a Storage Terminal on the same fiber. Autocrafting runs on your server racks: they lend compute (Pi 1, 1U 2, GPU 6, Quantum 20, ASIC none, and the specialists: Crafting Coprocessor 8, Crafting Accelerator 30) and stop mining while a job runs. In the terminal, middle-click a craftable item (marked +) to order more, even when some is in stock.
guide.rackcraft.chapter.utilities.intro: Big facilities make more than coin: spare power, waste heat and a thirst for fresh water. Three cube multiblocks (2x2x2 to 5x5x5, or 10x10x10 with research, like the nuclear machines) turn those into something useful. The Desalination Plant makes tower water from any water it touches, sea water included, and never drains it. The Grid-Tie Substation sells spare solar, wind and reactor power for RackCoin, cheap at midday and dear in the evening peak; it never touches batteries, diesel or the utility feed. The Heat Recovery Plant is a heat sink that sells your coolant loop's heat to nearby villages as district heating, 50 kW per villager, so the bigger the village the more it takes and pays.
guide.rackcraft.chapter.wiring.intro: Past the first hall, the work is routing. A Trunk Bundle carries power, coolant and fiber as one; the Cable Planner draws a run before you lay it; a Patch Panel rewires from a face click; Pylons and Power Beacons carry power where cable cannot go. The Constructor's Gauntlet and Terraformer Cannon do the heavy lifting by hand. Structured Cabling, Long Reach and Wireless Power in the R&D tab unlock the machines.
guide.rackcraft.entry.agi_weights: A thumb drive holding the weights of the AGI you trained. It left a copy in your outbox, presumably as a gesture of goodwill. It does nothing. It is watching. Do not open-source it.
guide.rackcraft.entry.aluminum_ingot: A light metal used for coolant pipes, fans, solar frames and cryogenic parts.
guide.rackcraft.entry.art_aggregate: Four children's drawings, scanned and tagged. Upload it to one of the image models (SketchDiffusion, Nano Melon, Nano Melon Pro) at an Operations Terminal.
guide.rackcraft.entry.art_table: Training data for the image model. Stock it with paper and Crayons and baby villagers come running to draw. Each kid finishes a drawing every 20 seconds (up to four kids); four drawings make a Crayon Art Aggregate. Kids at a stocked table never seem to grow up. Connect it to a Storage Array with Item Pipe and it restocks itself and sends the aggregates back to storage; hoppers work too.
guide.rackcraft.entry.asic_miner: A module built only to mine crypto. It draws 0.4 to 1.2 kW and mines 5 RC per second at full load, cheap for what it earns, but it runs hot. Like all tier 3 hardware it is water-cooled: it needs a Freshwater Pump on its rack's coolant network (1 unit).
guide.rackcraft.entry.assembly_arm: A robot arm with a gripper and nine slots of parts. Place it beside a Conveyor Belt, facing the belt, and stock it with what the line needs (Electric Motors, Circuit Boards, Hydrogen Canisters): it installs parts into every workpiece whose next step it can do, three seconds per step at 250 kW, and keeps going while the steps that follow are installs too. Hoppers and Item Pipes can restock it, and on an Item Pipe it fetches for itself: it watches the belt in front of it and the five before it, and takes whatever part the next workpiece needs from storage (or buys it, if an Auto-Buyer is on the network).
guide.rackcraft.entry.auto_buyer: The company credit card, in a box. Put it on a storage network (touching a Storage Array, a Storage Link, an Item Pipe or a machine that restocks from storage) and power it, and whenever a machine on that storage restocks and storage comes up short, it buys the difference at Crypto Exchange prices out of the RackCoin balance: generator fuel, Fuel Cells, process inputs, paper and ink, Repair Kits and replacement modules, Assembly Robot parts, site materials. A Diesel Generator with no fuel in storage gets the best fuel the Exchange sells. It can't buy what the Exchange doesn't sell: drones, hydrogen and Assembly Line products. Its screen shows what it has spent. Draws 2 kW.
guide.rackcraft.entry.battery_bank: Stores 3,000 kJ of surplus power, charging at up to 15 kW and discharging at up to 60 kW; it loses 10% of the energy going in and 10% coming out. Build Battery Banks into a solid cube, 2x2x2 up to 5x5x5 (or 10x10x10 with research), and they form a Grid-Scale Battery: one store holding every bank's charge and charging and discharging at every bank's rate, with 10% more capacity per bank for each step up in size (40% more in a 5-cube) and smaller losses, 8% each way for a 2-cube down to 2% for a 5-cube.
guide.rackcraft.entry.battery_cell: A fat little power cell for hand tools. The Constructor's Gauntlet and the Terraformer Cannon burn them. Not rechargeable; it was never going to be.
guide.rackcraft.entry.bauxite_ore: Reddish ore found between Y 0 and Y 64, in veins of up to seven blocks. Mine it with a stone pickaxe or better for Raw Bauxite; Fortune increases the drop and Silk Touch keeps the ore.
guide.rackcraft.entry.beacon_receiver: The catching end of a Power Beacon: it pairs with the nearest beacon in range and feeds whatever power network it touches, drawn before any other source. Out of range, it just sits there looking smug.
guide.rackcraft.entry.belt_loader: Feeds an Assembly Line straight from storage. Put it on an Item Pipe that reaches a Storage Array, face it at the first Conveyor Belt, and put one of the item you want in its slot (that one is only a sample and stays put). Whenever the belt in front is empty it takes another from storage and puts it on, up to one a second. Needs no power.
guide.rackcraft.entry.belt_unloader: Files whatever comes off the end of an Assembly Line into storage. Point the last Conveyor Belt into it and put it on an Item Pipe that reaches a Storage Array: finished drones, arrays, nacelles and the rest land in its nine-slot buffer and go into storage once a second. Hoppers can empty it too. Needs no power.
guide.rackcraft.entry.biodiesel_canister: Refined biomass in an aluminium can. It runs a Diesel Generator for 8 minutes, the best renewable fuel for backup power.
guide.rackcraft.entry.biomass_pellet: Compressed crop waste. Eight crops, seeds, leaves or saplings plus bone meal make four pellets, which each burn for 40 seconds. It is a renewable fuel for farms.
guide.rackcraft.entry.blade_chassis: An empty module sled: the base for every new module made on the Assembly Line. The first part an Assembly Robot fits decides what it becomes: GPU Chips make an FPGA Module, bronze Chiplets an NPU, silver Chiplets a Neuromorphic Core, gold Chiplets a Photonic Tensor Core, and Superconducting Wire a Quantum Annealer.
guide.rackcraft.entry.blank_pattern: Put one in the Storage Terminal's pattern slot, lay out a recipe on the crafting grid, and press Encode to make a Recipe Pattern.
guide.rackcraft.entry.blanking_panel: Seals gaps in a row of racks. Like the raised floor, it blocks airflow, which keeps hot exhaust air out of the cold aisle.
guide.rackcraft.entry.blueprint: A sheet of the future. Blank until a Blueprint Scanner writes a box of Rackcraft blocks into it: their kinds, which way they face, and for a rack the module that fills most of its bays. Put a written one in a Site Planner's material slots and pick the Blueprint layout, and the drones print it again wherever the site is.
guide.rackcraft.entry.blueprint_scanner: Use on a block for one corner and another for the opposite; the box is outlined while you hold it. Use in the air to scan it into a blank Blueprint in your inventory, up to 64 blocks a side. It only reads Rackcraft blocks (the printer's drones carry nothing else), and nothing inside machines but a rack's main module. Needs Digital Twin researched.
guide.rackcraft.entry.cable_planner: Draw a cable run before you lay it. Right-click a block face to set the start, another for the end: a ghost of the route hangs in the world, red where something is in the way. Right-click in the air to cycle the route style (Straight, Zig-zag, Shortest, Hug the Walls) and sneak-right-click in the air to cycle the cable kind, Use a block face a third time to lay the whole route, taking the cables from your inventory (or from a Wireless Terminal's storage). Sneak-use on a block to clear the route.
guide.rackcraft.entry.carbon_offset: Right-click to retire it. It removes exactly one point of smog where you stand, and an unknowable amount of guilt. Comes in packs of four, because one would look bad.
guide.rackcraft.entry.cask_sealer: Seals nuclear waste away for good: four Spent Fuel and four Depleted Uranium (the shielding) make one Sealed Waste Cask, a minute per batch per core, 15 kW per working core. A multiblock: build a solid cube of 2x2x2 up to 5x5x5 (or 10x10x10 with research).
guide.rackcraft.entry.cdu: Delivers liquid cooling directly to hardware. A Quantum Core only runs in a rack that has a CDU directly beside it. Draws 0.5 kW and sits on the coolant loop like a pipe.
guide.rackcraft.entry.chiller: Heavy-duty heat sink for a coolant loop: takes 250 kW out of the loop anywhere, indoors or out, with no water. It pays for it in power: 5 kW plus a fifth of the heat it moves (50 kW more at full tilt).
guide.rackcraft.entry.chiplet_bronze: A die cut from a wafer that tested slow. Once Chiplets and Advanced Packaging is researched, an Assembly Line dices a Wafer-Scale Engine (weld, two Graphene Sheets, rivet) into eight chiplets, and the whole wafer bins as one: 60% bronze, 30% silver, 10% gold. Bronze goes into HBM Stacks and NPU Inference Cards. A higher bin can always be crafted down to a lower one.
guide.rackcraft.entry.chiplet_gold: The silicon lottery's jackpot: only one wafer in ten bins gold. The Photonic Tensor Core needs two and the Quantum Annealer one. Craft it into a silver chiplet if you must, but you'll regret it.
guide.rackcraft.entry.chiplet_silver: A die that tested well: 30% of diced wafers bin silver. Neuromorphic Cores and Photonic Interconnects need silver. Craft one into a bronze chiplet if you need bronze more.
guide.rackcraft.entry.circuit_board: The universal electronics component used by almost every machine and module.
guide.rackcraft.entry.coke: Coal or charcoal baked in a blast furnace. It burns twice as long as coal: 160 seconds of diesel runtime.
guide.rackcraft.entry.coke_block: Nine pieces of coke pressed into a block. It burns for 1,600 seconds in a Diesel Generator, the longest-lasting fuel in the mod.
guide.rackcraft.entry.comms_satellite: Bus + 16 Copper Wire + 4 Circuit Boards, welded and riveted. One stage. In orbit, each one (up to five) makes Darknet parcels arrive 10% sooner and adds a Compute Lease slot.
guide.rackcraft.entry.construction_drone: A heavy-lift quadcopter in hazard stripes. Load it into a Site Planner and it clears sites, places Solar Arrays and Wind Towers, and lays cable, carrying its materials out from storage and bringing back whatever it cleared. Built on the Assembly Line from a Heavy Drone Frame.
guide.rackcraft.entry.constructor_gauntl: A powered glove that builds from a distance. It reaches 32 blocks, takes blocks from the storage network of a Wireless Terminal in your inventory and returns what it deletes there, and spends a Battery Cell for every 16 uses. Sneak-use in the air to cycle modes: Line, Plane, Box fill, Swap and Delete. Right-click a block to start a selection, again to finish it. Swap replaces every block in the box with the block in your off hand. Long Reach research stretches it to 128 blocks.
guide.rackcraft.entry.conveyor_belt: Carries one item at a time along the way it faces, a block a second. Drop an item on it, right-click it with one, or feed it with a hopper; right-click with an empty hand to take the item back. At the far end the item moves onto the next belt (which can turn), into a chest, hopper or any container, or drops off the end. A Robot Arm facing a belt stops whatever it can work on in the middle of that belt, does its step, and lets it go. Lay belts past a row of arms and you have an Assembly Line. Players and mobs standing on a running belt get carried too.
guide.rackcraft.entry.coolant_pipe: Each connected run of Coolant Pipe is one coolant loop. Heat goes in from racks with liquid-cooled modules, Rear-Door Coolers, CRAC units and Modular Reactors, and comes out at heat sinks: Cooling Towers, Dry Coolers, Chillers and Water Heat Exchangers. Run it as far as you like, so the heat can be dumped well away from the racks. Check a loop with the Multimeter: heat in versus what its sinks can take.
guide.rackcraft.entry.cooling_tower: Heat sink for a coolant loop. It takes 120 kW of heat out of the loop when a Freshwater Pump on the same loop supplies it 4 units of water, and only 20 kW dry. It drinks the lake: the water it uses drains source blocks from the pump's shore. Draws 4 kW.
guide.rackcraft.entry.copper_wire: One copper ingot makes six wires. Wire goes into circuit boards, scanners and repair kits.
guide.rackcraft.entry.core_router: A backbone router that provides 1,000 units of bandwidth, enough for a full hall of GPU blades and quantum cores.
guide.rackcraft.entry.cpu_chip: A general-purpose processor. Two CPUs make a GPU chip.
guide.rackcraft.entry.crac_unit: Computer-room air conditioner: takes heat out of the room air and puts it into its coolant loop. It pulls up to 40 kW from the air on each of its front and back faces, more the hotter that air is. Its loop needs sinks to take that heat. Draws 3 kW.
guide.rackcraft.entry.crafting_accelerat: The heavy autocrafting module: 30 general compute (five GPU Blades' worth) for 3.5 kW. It is liquid-cooled, so its rack must be on a coolant loop with a heat sink. It can't mine and lends only 2 AI compute. Boots in 8 seconds.
guide.rackcraft.entry.crafting_coprocess: A rack module built for autocrafting: 8 general compute (four 1U Servers' worth) for 0.9 kW, and air-cooled, so it needs no coolant loop. It can't mine, and lends only 0.5 AI compute. Racks full of them turn a Storage Terminal's job queue into a production line. Boots in 4 seconds.
guide.rackcraft.entry.crayons: A box of wax crayons for the Kids' Art Table. Lasts 64 drawings.
guide.rackcraft.entry.creative_cooler: Creative only. Holds the air cells in front of and behind it at the temperature you set, regardless of how much heat is dumped there. Air never goes below the ambient temperature (24 C by default). Right-click to set the target in C.
guide.rackcraft.entry.creative_power: Creative only. Supplies as much power as you set, forever, to the power network it touches. Right-click to set the output in kW (needs creative mode or operator).
guide.rackcraft.entry.creative_rack: Creative only. Mines RackCoin at the rate you set, with no modules, power, fiber or cooling needed. It can also draw a set load from its power network, which makes it a test load for generators. Right-click to set both values.
guide.rackcraft.entry.creative_router: Creative only. Gives its fiber network as much bandwidth as you set. Right-click to change it.
guide.rackcraft.entry.cryo_coil: An aluminium coil packed in blue ice that keeps a Quantum Core near absolute zero.
guide.rackcraft.entry.cryostat: Keeps Quantum Annealers a whisker above absolute zero. A rack holding Annealers only runs with a cold Cryostat directly beside it: one with power (15 kW) and Hydrogen Canisters in its slot. The liquid hydrogen boils off as it works, one canister every 5 minutes for each running Annealer beside it (a rack between two Cryostats splits the load). On an Item Pipe it keeps sixteen canisters from storage or a Hydrogen Tank. Can't be bought.
guide.rackcraft.entry.crypto_exchange: Spend the RackCoin your racks have mined. Pick a tab, then click an offer to buy it; Shift-click buys ten. The screen shows your balance and live mining rate, and hovering an offer you can't afford yet tells you how long until you can. It needs no power or cables: every rack in the world pays into one shared balance.
guide.rackcraft.entry.cvd_furnace: Grows Graphene Sheets by chemical vapour deposition: four Coke and a Hydrogen Canister make two sheets, a minute per batch per core, 150 kW per working core. A multiblock like the other processing cubes (2x2x2 and up), fed and emptied by hand, hopper or Item Pipe; on a pipe to a Hydrogen Tank it draws its hydrogen from the tank. It does nothing until Advanced Materials is researched.
guide.rackcraft.entry.darknet_terminal: An auction house for things the Exchange won't sell: enchanted books, spawn eggs, empty spawners (right-click one with a spawn egg), elytras, nether stars, the odd dragon egg, and now and then anything else. Four auctions run at a time; more listing slots cost a fortune. Bid with RackCoin: a bid is paid when you place it and refunded if you're outbid. Rival bidders want the lot too and answer within seconds. An auction closes one minute after the first player bid, or after fifteen minutes if nobody bids, and the highest bidder wins. Won lots ship to the terminal's dead drop two to six minutes later. It needs no power: the seven proxies are someone else's problem.
guide.rackcraft.entry.depleted_uranium: What the Gas Centrifuge leaves behind: dense, heavy and good at stopping radiation. A Cask Sealer uses it to shield Spent Fuel.
guide.rackcraft.entry.desalination_plant: Makes fresh water for Cooling Towers out of any water it touches, the sea included. A multiblock: build a solid cube of 2x2x2 up to 5x5x5 (or 10x10x10 with research) with water against its outside. Each core supplies 2 units of fresh water to the towers on its coolant loop (a tower wants 4) and draws 20 kW, less per core in bigger cubes. Unlike a Freshwater Pump it never drains anything, so a coastal campus can run towers forever.
guide.rackcraft.entry.diesel_generator: Backup generator that delivers 40 kW. It spins up only when demand exceeds solar, wind, reactor and utility supply, and takes 10 seconds to get there. It burns any furnace fuel plus Rackcraft fuels from its slot, only while it is actually supplying power. Open it to watch its output, fuel and spin-up live; it smokes while running and vents 4 kW of heat out of its radiator at the back.
guide.rackcraft.entry.dimensional_shard: A Linked Shard with a Nether Star in it. It entangles pads in different dimensions, which cost twenty times the power and four times the hydrogen to jump between.
guide.rackcraft.entry.drive_1k: Hot storage for 1,024 items of any mix of types. Goes in a Storage Array. Its contents stay with the drive, so you can move it to another array.
guide.rackcraft.entry.drone_dock: Home base for Maintenance Drones, and the end of walking to every broken thing in a big hall. Load drones into its first slot (up to eight), Hydrogen Canisters into the second, and spares into the rest: rack modules and Repair Kits. Better, put it on an Item Pipe that reaches storage: it then takes drones, hydrogen, Repair Kits and replacement modules from storage as it needs them, always the same kind of module that failed, and files the dead ones away. Every couple of seconds it looks for work within 32 blocks across (and 96 up or down, so a Wind Tower's nacelle is in reach) and sends a drone to each job: swapping a Failed Module out of a rack for a spare (the dead one comes back to the dock), splicing a cut cable with a Repair Kit, resetting a tripped PDU breaker, or servicing a worn Solar Array or Wind Tower. Each trip burns an eighth of a canister. Draws 2 kW. Hit a drone and it drops as an item, so maybe don't.
guide.rackcraft.entry.drone_frame: The bare airframe of a Maintenance Drone. Put it on an Assembly Line: an Assembly Robot fits four Electric Motors, a Welding Robot welds the mounts, Assembly Robots fit two Circuit Boards and a Hydrogen Canister, and a Riveting Robot closes the shell. A frame that falls off the line half-built remembers how far it got; its tooltip says what it needs next.
guide.rackcraft.entry.dry_cooler: Heat sink for a coolant loop that needs no water: big fans blow outside air across a radiator. It takes 40 kW out of the loop in temperate biomes, 60 kW in snowy ones and only 24 kW in deserts, savannas and badlands. Draws 2 kW.
guide.rackcraft.entry.dyson_mirror: Bus + 16 Solar Panels, welded and riveted. Three stages. One more mirror in the swarm around the sun: each beams 2 MW down to your Rectennas, forever. It takes a lot of hydrogen to put one up and a long time to pay it back, which is rather the point of a Dyson swarm.
guide.rackcraft.entry.electric_motor: Copper windings around an iron core in a steel can. Conveyor Belts and robot arms run on them, and a Maintenance Drone needs four for its rotors.
guide.rackcraft.entry.electrolyser: Splits water into hydrogen with an absurd amount of electricity: each core rolls an Aluminium Ingot into a tank and fills it, one Hydrogen Canister every 30 seconds, drawing 4,000 kW while it works. With a Hydrogen Tank touching it (or on the same Item Pipe or Storage Link network) it fills the tank instead, with no ingots at all, and stops only when the tanks are full. A multiblock: build a solid cube of 2x2x2 to 5x5x5 (or 10x10x10 with research) with water against its outside (any water, sea water too; it is never used up). A 3x3x3 pulls close to 100 MW and a 5x5x5 about 400 MW, so this is where a finished facility's spare power goes. Bigger cubes use up to 20% less power per core. Hydrogen fuels Maintenance Drones, and it is the rocket fuel for the launch programme. Feed and empty it like the other processing cubes; canisters gather in the port.
guide.rackcraft.entry.enriched_uranium: Reactor-grade uranium from a Gas Centrifuge. A Fuel Fabricator makes a Fuel Cell from one, with two Steel Ingots.
guide.rackcraft.entry.epitaxy_reactor: Recovers the trace of gallium in bauxite and grows it into crystal: eight Raw Bauxite and a Hydrogen Canister make one Gallium Nitride, 90 seconds per batch per core, 250 kW per working core. A processing cube (2x2x2 and up), locked until Advanced Materials is researched.
guide.rackcraft.entry.ewaste_recycler: Shreds dead hardware back into parts: each Failed Module gives three Silicon and a Copper Wire, fifteen seconds per batch per core, 10 kW per working core. A multiblock: build a solid cube of 2x2x2 up to 5x5x5 (or 10x10x10 with research). Pairs well with hardware failure events and an Item Pipe. Products gather in the port, the marked corner block.
guide.rackcraft.entry.exascale_cabinet: Tier 4: twenty-four bays on a photonic fabric. Everything in it mines and lends compute 20% faster, its mining needs only half the fiber bandwidth, and like an immersion rack all its heat goes to the loop. It only takes tier 2 hardware and up (no Pi Nodes, 1U Servers, ASIC Miners or Crafting Coprocessors), and its switches draw 30 kW whenever it has anything in it. Built on the Assembly Line from a Liquid-Immersion Rack with eight Photonic Interconnects, four Superconducting Wire, a Core Router and four HBM Stacks, once Exascale Architecture is researched.
guide.rackcraft.entry.exhaust_fan: Pulls hot air out of the block in front of it and dumps it outside: up to 10 kW, only while that air is at least 1 C above ambient, so it idles (and stays clean) when there's nothing to move. Point it into a hot aisle. Moving heat outside makes smog in proportion to the heat moved; smog spreads to neighbouring chunks and dims solar panels, and past 30 it makes you dizzy, then come spells of blindness, a hacking cough, and from 70 poison. Wear a Respirator or run a Smog Scrubber. Draws 0.2 kW.
guide.rackcraft.entry.facility_controlle: The operations desk. It shows credits, availability, the active contract and any running event, and sells parts for RackCoin. Players within 64 blocks of a controller are alerted when an event starts.
guide.rackcraft.entry.failed_module: Dead hardware. Recycle it in a blast furnace to recover Silicon.
guide.rackcraft.entry.fiber_cable: Connects racks to routers, controllers and monitoring walls. Racks only earn credits over fiber that reaches a router.
guide.rackcraft.entry.field_manual: This book. Right-click it to open. Click any Rackcraft ingredient in a recipe to jump to its page.
guide.rackcraft.entry.fire_suppression_t: Holds a Suppression Canister in its single slot, ready for the facility's fire protection.
guide.rackcraft.entry.fpga_module: Reprogrammable hardware: right-click it to reflash it for mining (8 RC/s), AI (8 AI compute) or autocrafting (20 general compute), about two thirds of what the specialist module does in each. Draws 0.4 to 2.5 kW and is air-cooled. Take it out of the rack to reflash it. Built on the Assembly Line from a Blade Chassis (two GPU Chips, two Graphene Sheets, two RAM Modules, weld, rivet) once Advanced Materials is researched.
guide.rackcraft.entry.freshwater_pump: Supplies fresh water to the Cooling Towers on its coolant loop. Place it touching a lake or river; ocean and beach water is salt and won't do. It draws 1.5 kW and supplies one unit per three water source blocks within six blocks, up to 16 units: four towers' worth. It drinks the lake: every four minutes of one unit drains a source block from the shore. Only towers need water; Dry Coolers, Chillers and Water Heat Exchangers don't.
guide.rackcraft.entry.fuel_cell: The fuel for the Modular Reactor: one cell runs a reactor for 30 minutes at full output and leaves a Spent Fuel rod behind. It can't be crafted or bought: a Fuel Fabricator makes it from Enriched Uranium. Item Pipes can deliver them from storage.
guide.rackcraft.entry.fuel_fabricator: The only way to make Fuel Cells: one Enriched Uranium and two Steel Ingots make one cell, a minute per batch per core, 30 kW per working core. A multiblock: build a solid cube of 2x2x2 up to 5x5x5 (or 10x10x10 with research).
guide.rackcraft.entry.gallium_nitride: A blue-violet crystal grown in an Epitaxy Reactor from bauxite's gallium. The base of a Photonic Interconnect. Can't be bought.
guide.rackcraft.entry.gas_centrifuge: Enriches uranium: spins six Yellowcake into one Enriched Uranium and four Depleted Uranium, two minutes per batch per core, 60 kW per working core. A multiblock: build a solid cube of 2x2x2 up to 5x5x5 (or 10x10x10 with research) Gas Centrifuges (a real cascade, and a real power bill).
guide.rackcraft.entry.generated_document: AI-generated writing: essays, homework, legal documents and worse. It remembers its prompt and quality, so a spare can fill a repeat order.
guide.rackcraft.entry.generated_image: An AI-generated image, made for a contract. It remembers its prompt and quality: keep spares, because clients often ask for the same thing again.
guide.rackcraft.entry.gpu_blade: An accelerator card. It draws 1 to 3 kW and mines 12 RC per second at full load. Plan for its heat. Water-cooled: it needs 2 units from a Freshwater Pump. It also lends 10 AI compute to contract work, which pays a little better than mining.
guide.rackcraft.entry.gpu_chip: A diamond-tipped parallel processor for GPU blades, quantum cores and core routers.
guide.rackcraft.entry.graphene_sheet: Carbon one atom thick: stronger than steel, better at heat than copper. Only a CVD Furnace makes it, from Coke and hydrogen. Goes into FPGAs, HBM Stacks, Neuromorphic Cores, wafer dicing and Liquid-Immersion Racks. Can't be bought.
guide.rackcraft.entry.grapple_hook: Use it to fire a hook at the block you are looking at, up to 40 blocks away, and be pulled to it, faster as you go. Sneak to let go. It burns a Battery Cell a shot, and the last bit of the fall at the end is cushioned.
guide.rackcraft.entry.grid_substation: Sells your spare power to the outside grid for RackCoin. A multiblock: build a solid cube of 2x2x2 up to 5x5x5 (or 10x10x10 with research) on your power network. Each core exports up to 1 MW, but only what solar panels, wind turbines and reactors have left over once everything else is powered and the batteries are charged: it never drains a battery, runs a diesel or resells the utility feed. It pays 0.05 RC per kJ at night, 60% of that at midday when every solar farm is selling, and two and a half times as much in the evening peak. Exported reactor power still burns fuel.
guide.rackcraft.entry.hbm_stack: Four memory dies stacked on a chiplet and bonded with graphene. Built on the Assembly Line from a RAM Module: three more RAM Modules, a bronze Chiplet and a Graphene Sheet, then riveted. Every tier 3 and 4 module and the Exascale Cabinet use them.
guide.rackcraft.entry.heat_recovery_plan: District heating: a heat sink on your coolant loop that sells the heat to the villages around it. A multiblock: build a solid cube of 2x2x2 up to 5x5x5 (or 10x10x10 with research) and pipe it into a loop. Every villager within 64 blocks takes 50 kW (half again in cold biomes, less in hot ones), up to 400 kW per core, and pays 0.4 RC per kJ for it. It needs no power and no water, just customers, so a well-stocked village next door is worth more than you'd think.
guide.rackcraft.entry.heavy_drone_frame: A bigger airframe for drones that lift things. What it becomes depends on the first part an Assembly Robot fits: two Sticky Pistons make a Construction Drone, a Diamond Shovel a Terraforming Drone. Either way it then gets four Electric Motors, two Circuit Boards, a weld and rivets.
guide.rackcraft.entry.high_density_rack: Tier 2: twelve module bays and a rear-door cooler built into its back. On a coolant loop, the door catches up to 40 kW of the rack's hot air into the loop before it reaches the room, on top of the 85% that liquid-cooled modules send down the pipe; off a loop it is just a bigger rack. Its fans draw 0.5 kW. It can't be crafted: an Assembly Robot fits a Server Rack with two Cryo Coils, a CDU and a Rear-Door Cooler, then it is welded and riveted, once High-Density Racks is researched.
guide.rackcraft.entry.hydrogen_canister: An aluminium tank of compressed hydrogen from an Electrolyser: about 120 MJ of electricity went into it. A Drone Dock burns one every eight trips, an Assembly Robot can fit one into a drone as its fuel tank, and a launch pad will want them by the thousand.
guide.rackcraft.entry.hydrogen_jetpack: A chestplate with a thrust bottle. Hold jump to climb, sneak in the air to hover (half the fuel), sprint while climbing to boost. It burns a Hydrogen Canister for every thirty seconds of thrust, taken from the canisters you carry or a Wireless Terminal's storage. Run dry in a long fall and it vents the last of its gas once, every five minutes, to slow you down. Inert until Personal Propulsion is researched.
guide.rackcraft.entry.hydrogen_tank: Holds hydrogen as gas, once Cryogenic Hydrogen Storage is researched. Each block holds 256 canisters' worth, and a solid cube (2x2x2 up to 5x5x5, or 10x10x10 with research) holds more per block: 40% more in a 5x5x5. An Electrolyser touching a tank, or on the same Item Pipe or Storage Link network, pipes its hydrogen straight in and needs no Aluminium Ingots. Storage counts the tank's hydrogen as Hydrogen Canisters, so Drone Docks, Site Planners, Launch Controls and anything else that takes canisters from storage draw on the tank. Its slot holds Tanker Drones, which carry hydrogen to docks, planners and Launch Controls up to 256 blocks away. Needs no power.
guide.rackcraft.entry.immersion_rack: Tier 3: sixteen bays, with every module sunk in dielectric fluid. All of its heat goes into the coolant loop and none into the air, so a hall of them needs no CRACs or fans at all, only sinks. It won't run off a loop, even with air-cooled modules in it, and its pumps draw 2 kW. Built on the Assembly Line from a High-Density Rack, two CDUs, eight Coolant Pipe and four Graphene Sheets, once Immersion Cooling is researched.
guide.rackcraft.entry.item_pipe: Moves items between storage and the machines that use them. Connect Storage Arrays or Tape Libraries to Kids' Art Tables, Scriptorium Desks, Diesel Generators and Modular Reactors: once a second they are topped up from storage (paper, crayons, ink, fuel, Fuel Cells) and finished Art Aggregates and Text Corpora go back in. It is its own network, separate from fiber.
guide.rackcraft.entry.launch_control: Runs the launch programme. Place it touching a 3x3 Launch Pad. Load Rocket Stages into its first three slots, a payload into the fourth, and Hydrogen Canisters into the fifth (hoppers and Item Pipes work): canisters are drained into its tank, which holds 4,096. Each stage burns 128 canisters. Comms and Survey Satellites need one stage, an Orbital Data Center two, a Dyson Mirror three. Press Launch, and after a ten-second countdown the rocket lifts off. About one launch in fifty ends in a rapid unscheduled disassembly: the stages and fuel are lost, but the payload's abort motor brings it back. Draws 5 kW, and needs power to launch.
guide.rackcraft.entry.launch_pad: Blast-proof concrete with a flame trench. Lay nine in a flat 3x3 square with open sky above the middle, put a Launch Control beside it, and you have a spaceport. The rocket stands on the centre block.
guide.rackcraft.entry.launch_tower: Red steel lattice for building the service tower beside a launch pad, the way the big rockets had one. It does nothing but look the part, and you can see through it. Stack it as high as your rocket.
guide.rackcraft.entry.linked_shard: Half of an entangled pair, waiting for a pad. Use it on a Quantum Teleport Pad, then on a second one, and the two are entangled and the shard is used up. Sneak-use it on a pad to cut its pair.
guide.rackcraft.entry.maglev_rail: A slim rail for a Mag-Lev line. Rails and Stations that touch form a line a car can run along, and a rail is also a power-network block, so it carries power from any cable it touches. A cut rail breaks the line: a Repair Kit splices it. Inert until Magnetic Levitation is researched.
guide.rackcraft.entry.maglev_station: Where a line starts and ends. Right-click to ride to its destination (the nearest station until you choose); sneak-right-click with an empty hand to cycle destinations down the line. The car carries one rider, glides at up to 54 blocks a second, and draws 800 kW from this station's network while it runs: under 10% of that and it stalls, with an apology. Break a rail ahead of it and it stops there. Draws 0.5 kW otherwise.
guide.rackcraft.entry.maintenance_drone: A quadcopter with a gripper and a strong sense of duty. Load it into a Drone Dock and it flies out to fix things on its own: failed rack modules, cut cables and tripped breakers. It is built on an Assembly Line, not a crafting table.
guide.rackcraft.entry.modular_reactor: A small modular reactor: 500 kW of steady power, burning one Fuel Cell every 30 minutes at full output (less at part load), and every spent cell comes out as Spent Fuel in its waste slot. Build reactors into a solid cube, 2x2x2 up to 5x5x5 (or 10x10x10 with research), and they form one reactor array: the casing changes to show it, the output of every core adds up, fuel and waste are shared evenly across every core's slots, and each core burns 5% (2-cube) up to 20% (5-cube) less fuel. When the waste slots are full the reactor stops: seal the Spent Fuel into casks. Its heat, 30% of its output, goes into its coolant loop if piped, otherwise into the air.
guide.rackcraft.entry.monitoring_wall: A wall display for the fiber network. Open it to see facility power, the hottest inlet and total load.
guide.rackcraft.entry.multimeter: Right-click any machine or cable for a live readout: power delivered against demand, generator fuel, battery charge, rack mining status, and fiber bandwidth. Sneak-right-click a machine to rotate it.
guide.rackcraft.entry.nacelle_frame: The empty shell of a Wind Tower Nacelle. On an Assembly Line it gets 8 Electric Motors (the generator), 4 Circuit Boards, a weld, 16 Copper Wire and rivets.
guide.rackcraft.entry.neuromorphic_core: Spiking silicon modelled on a brain: 80 general compute for autocrafting and general research on just 0.2 to 1.2 kW, air-cooled. It can't mine and lends little AI. Built on the Assembly Line from a Blade Chassis (two silver Chiplets, an HBM Stack, two Graphene Sheets, weld, rivet) once Chiplets and Advanced Packaging is researched.
guide.rackcraft.entry.npu_card: An inference accelerator: 32 AI compute on 0.3 to 1.8 kW, air-cooled, but only for contract generation and Compute Leases. It never helps train models, R&D or frontier runs. It can't mine. Built on the Assembly Line from a Blade Chassis (four bronze Chiplets, an HBM Stack, two Circuit Boards, rivet) once Chiplets and Advanced Packaging is researched.
guide.rackcraft.entry.operations_termina: Runs the whole facility from one screen: the AI contract board (accept, pick a model, generate, deliver), what every cluster of racks is doing and its policy, the model lineup and each model's training, RackCoin income, and every problem with racks, storage, pumps, cables, generators and smog in this dimension. It needs no power or cables.
guide.rackcraft.entry.orbital_datacenter: Bus + 4 Wafer-Scale Engines + 4 Cryo Coils, welded and riveted. Two stages. Up there the sun never sets and space is cold: every module in orbit adds 3% to the AI and general compute of every rack you own. There is no limit, and repeatable research never stops wanting more.
guide.rackcraft.entry.patch_panel: Rewire without touching a cable. Each of its six faces has a port number from 0 to 8: cables and machines on two faces with the same port (not 0) are joined, on every network at once; a face on port 0 is isolated. Right-click a face with an empty hand to cycle its port, use a Name Tag to label the panel, and read the wiring with a Multimeter. It carries nothing itself, so a panel with every face on port 0 is a very expensive wall. Inert until Structured Cabling is researched.
guide.rackcraft.entry.pdu: A distribution point on the power network. Open it to see draw and satisfaction, and use Reset Breaker to clear a tripped breaker.
guide.rackcraft.entry.photonic_chip: Moves data as light. Built on the Assembly Line from Gallium Nitride once Silicon Photonics is researched: a silver Chiplet, four Fiber Cable, welded and riveted. Four go in a Photonic Tensor Core and eight in an Exascale Cabinet.
guide.rackcraft.entry.photonic_tensor_co: Matrix maths done in light: 300 AI compute and 60 general compute in one bay, twice a Wafer-Scale Engine, on 3 to 12 kW. Liquid-cooled; it can't mine. Built on the Assembly Line from a Blade Chassis (two gold Chiplets, four Photonic Interconnects, two HBM Stacks, weld, rivet) once Silicon Photonics is researched. Hardware failures never take one out.
guide.rackcraft.entry.pi_node: A starter module. It draws 0.05 to 0.15 kW and mines 0.5 RC per second at full load.
guide.rackcraft.entry.pod_port: Turns a solid block of High-Density Racks or better into a Compute Pod. Build a solid cuboid of at least four racks (no more than 2 x 4 x 8, and 64 in all), touch it with a powered Pod Port, and put Photonic Interconnects in its slot, one for every four racks: the fabric then lends 10% more AI compute from 4 racks, 20% from 8 and 30% from 16. The cost is one breaker: if any rack in the pod overheats, the whole pod trips and lends nothing until every rack has cooled. Its screen fills and empties every bay in the pod at once. Draws 0.5 kW. Inert until Compute Pods is researched.
guide.rackcraft.entry.power_beacon: Beams power through the air to any Beacon Receiver within 16 blocks, no cable needed. It draws what the receivers' network asks for, up to 1 MW, plus 15% lost to the sky. Receivers are shared out evenly, and a beam is a line of sparks you can follow. Needs Wireless Power.
guide.rackcraft.entry.power_cable: Links generators, batteries, PDUs and loads into one power network. Every machine touching the same connected cable run shares power. Cable cut events sever a segment; right-click it with a Repair Kit to splice it.
guide.rackcraft.entry.procurement_wall: A Monitoring Wall that has been to business school. Plug it into the same power grid as your Site Planners and it keeps their books: every purchase their drones make at the Crypto Exchange, itemised (what, how many, what each cost, what part of the job it was for, how long ago), with running totals per planner. It also shows a planner's price quote, and a button to approve it without walking over to the planner. Switch on its HUD and a live ledger of the latest purchases sits on your screen whenever you are within 48 blocks of a powered wall. Draws 0.5 kW.
guide.rackcraft.entry.pylon: A lattice mast for long-span power. Link two Pylons up to 128 blocks apart with a Pylon Linker and they behave as one cable, without a cable between them: a faint line of sparks shows the span. Every link wastes 3% of the network's load per 64 blocks of span. Both ends must be loaded to carry power, and a mast with an unloaded partner just carries nothing. Needs Structured Cabling.
guide.rackcraft.entry.pylon_linker: Use it on a Pylon, then on another, to string a span between them. Sneak-use on a linked Pylon to cut its spans. Range 128 blocks, or 256 between two Superconducting Pylons.
guide.rackcraft.entry.quantum_annealer: The best miner there is: 120 RC/s, twice a Quantum Core, on 4 to 14 kW, liquid-cooled. Its rack only runs with a cold Cryostat directly beside it, and each running Annealer boils off a Hydrogen Canister every 5 minutes. It boots in 25 seconds. Built on the Assembly Line from a Blade Chassis (four Superconducting Wire, a gold Chiplet, four Cryo Coils, an HBM Stack, weld, rivet) once Quantum Annealing is researched. Hardware failures never take one out.
guide.rackcraft.entry.quantum_core: The endgame module. It draws 3 to 9 kW and mines 60 RC per second, but only runs when a CDU is directly beside its rack. On top of its CDU it needs 4 units of freshwater cooling from a pump.
guide.rackcraft.entry.raised_floor_tile: A perforated floor panel that blocks airflow. Use it to seal the floor between hot and cold aisles so rack exhaust cannot creep back into the intakes.
guide.rackcraft.entry.ram_module: Memory for servers and GPU blades. Each one needs a gold ingot.
guide.rackcraft.entry.raw_bauxite: Unrefined aluminium ore. Smelt it in a furnace, or twice as fast in a blast furnace, to get Aluminum Ingots.
guide.rackcraft.entry.raw_uranium: Uranium ore straight out of the ground. Feed it to a Uranium Mill to make Yellowcake.
guide.rackcraft.entry.rear_door_cooler: A radiator door for the back of a rack. Place it against a rack's back face and it catches up to 40 kW of the rack's hot exhaust and puts it into its coolant loop instead of the room; anything left comes out of its far side. The simplest way to keep a big rack from cooking its neighbours. Draws 0.3 kW.
guide.rackcraft.entry.recipe_pattern: An encoded crafting recipe. Store it anywhere in the network and its output becomes autocraftable; the planner chains patterns together for multi-step recipes.
guide.rackcraft.entry.rectenna: Catches the power your Dyson Mirrors beam down from orbit. Each mirror sends 2 MW, shared out between every Rectenna in the dimension that can see the sky, up to 20 MW per Rectenna. It works day and night, never runs out and can't be sold through a Grid-Tie Substation. Without mirrors in orbit it does nothing.
guide.rackcraft.entry.repair_kit: Right-click a cut cable to splice it back together. Each kit holds 8 repairs.
guide.rackcraft.entry.respirator: A half-face mask with charcoal filters, worn in the helmet slot. While you wear it smog can't touch you: no dizziness, blindness, cough or poison. The filter clogs in smog (about 40 minutes of it, faster when it's choking); repair it with charcoal on an anvil.
guide.rackcraft.entry.riveting_arm: A robot arm with a pneumatic rivet gun. Place it beside a Conveyor Belt, facing the belt, and it rivets every workpiece that needs riveting as it passes: four seconds a job, drawing 600 kW while it hammers and 1 kW waiting. Loud.
guide.rackcraft.entry.rocket_stage: A finished rocket stage. Load it into a Launch Control. Payloads need one to three stages, and every stage burns 128 Hydrogen Canisters.
guide.rackcraft.entry.satellite_bus: The chassis every payload is built on. What it becomes depends on the first part an Assembly Robot fits: copper wire makes a Comms Satellite, a Thermal Scanner a Survey Satellite, Wafer-Scale Engines an Orbital Data Center, Solar Panels a Dyson Mirror.
guide.rackcraft.entry.server_1u: A workhorse module. It draws 0.2 to 0.6 kW and mines 2 RC per second at full load.
guide.rackcraft.entry.server_rack: The heart of the facility, with eight module bays: any module fits any bay, one per bay, so a rack takes eight GPU Blades as happily as eight Pi Nodes. Air comes in the front and every kilowatt it draws comes out as heat: out of the back as hot air, or, for liquid-cooled modules, 85% of it down its coolant pipe. A rack mines RackCoin (RC) when powered, networked by fiber to a router, and kept cool. Its screen shows the live mining rate or exactly what is stopping it, and where its heat is going. Use the 25/50/75/100% buttons to cap its load.
guide.rackcraft.entry.shackles: Use on a librarian near a free Scriptorium Desk to chain them to it. You can see the chain from their wrists to the desk. Only librarians can write.
guide.rackcraft.entry.silicon: Blast Nether Quartz to make it, or recycle a Failed Module. It is the base material for every chip.
guide.rackcraft.entry.silicon_foundry: Melts quartz and sand into silicon by the bucketload: two Nether Quartz and four Sand make eight Silicon, twenty seconds per batch per core, 40 kW per working core. A multiblock: build a solid cube of 2x2x2 up to 5x5x5 (or 10x10x10 with research). Handy for feeding a Wafer Fab, which eats sixteen Silicon an engine. Products gather in the port, the marked corner block.
guide.rackcraft.entry.site_planner: Builds whole power plants while you do something else. Mark a site with a Survey Stake (up to 48 x 48, within 96 blocks), use the stake on the planner, pick a layout (Solar Field, Tracking Solar Field, Wind Farm, Data Hall or Reactor Cube) and press Start. Construction Drones clear the site first: grass, flowers, snow, leaves and entire trees go into storage. Terraforming Drones then level it to its median height, five blocks a trip, and dock once it is even. Then the Construction Drones build: arrays packed edge to edge, or Wind Towers six blocks apart with their nacelles at Y 130. Last, they lay Power Cable between the towers and back to the planner, so put the planner on the grid you want the site on. The Reactor Cube layout builds solid cubes of Modular Reactors, a layer at a time, a block of air between cubes: press the Cube button to pick 2 x 2 x 2 up to 10 x 10 x 10 (as big as your Reactor Array research and the site allow). The Exchange sells the reactors, at machine prices, so the bill gets large. Slots: Construction Drones, Terraforming Drones, Hydrogen Canisters, then six for materials; on an Item Pipe it takes all of these from storage too. Switch on Docks and, once the site is built, it places as few Drone Docks as cover every array and tower (from storage, or bought at the Exchange), stocks them with Maintenance Drones and hydrogen from storage, and keeps them topped up. Switch on Buy and it pays for anything else it is short of (cable, fill) at the Crypto Exchange's prices; the Exchange doesn't sell arrays, tower parts, drones or hydrogen. Before the drones buy anything, the planner works out the whole bill and tells you item by item, once per job: nothing is bought until you press Approve. Every purchase is then written to a ledger that a Procurement Wall on the same grid will show you. Each trip burns a sixteenth of a canister. Draws 5 kW. Inside the site it moves anything without a block entity, so don't mark out your house; outside it, the cable only digs through earth and rock.
guide.rackcraft.entry.smog_scrubber: Pulls smog back out of the air: at full power it removes 1.5 smog per second from its own chunk and 0.75 from each neighbouring chunk. It draws 6 kW, so it is cheaper than the poison. Place it near your exhaust fans.
guide.rackcraft.entry.solar_array: Six panels' worth of solar on one 3x2 frame, built on the Assembly Line. Place it like a bed: it takes three blocks to your right and two ahead, and needs them clear. In full sun it makes 36 kW (smog dims it, night stops it) and every array touching another shares its power, so a field of them needs no cables. It slowly wears down, losing up to 30% over three days of running, until a Maintenance Drone from a Drone Dock services it. Break any part and the whole array comes up as one item.
guide.rackcraft.entry.solar_array_frame: The bare 3x2 frame of a Solar Array. On an Assembly Line it gets 6 Solar Panels, 2 Circuit Boards, a weld and rivets.
guide.rackcraft.entry.solar_array_tracki: A Solar Array sent back down the Assembly Line for motors and a controller, so its panels follow the sun. It makes 30% more than a fixed array, and keeps working at 60% through dawn and dusk when a fixed one is dark. Places, chains and wears like a Solar Array.
guide.rackcraft.entry.solar_panel: Produces up to 4 kW in daylight when the block above it can see the sky. Output scales with sky light. A solar panel is the first source drawn on in any network.
guide.rackcraft.entry.spent_fuel: A burnt-out Fuel Cell, and very much still radioactive. Carrying it gives you Radiation Sickness, worse the more you carry. Pipe it out of the reactor into storage and on to a Cask Sealer, which seals four of them into a Waste Cask.
guide.rackcraft.entry.stage_frame: An empty rocket stage: tanks and an engine mount with nothing in them. On an Assembly Line it gets a weld, four Electric Motors (turbopumps), two Circuit Boards (avionics), another weld and rivets, and comes off as a Rocket Stage.
guide.rackcraft.entry.steel_block: Compact storage for nine Steel Ingots. Heavy builds such as the Core Router, Modular Reactor and Quantum Core use it as a structural frame.
guide.rackcraft.entry.steel_ingot: Iron refined in a blast furnace. It forms the chassis of nearly every machine.
guide.rackcraft.entry.storage_array: Eight bays for Storage Drives. Like a rack it needs power (0.4 kW plus 0.15 kW per drive), takes cool air in the front and exhausts heat out the back. Link it to a Storage Terminal with Fiber Cable. If it loses power or reaches 40 C, its drives go offline until fixed; nothing is lost.
guide.rackcraft.entry.storage_exporter: Sends items from storage into whatever it faces. Put it on an Item Pipe that reaches a Storage Array, face it at a machine or container (a Site Planner, a Launch Control, a chest), and put samples of what to send in its nine slots: once a second it tops the block in front up to a stack of each, through the face it touches, so a machine only gets what its slots take. The samples stay put. Needs no power.
guide.rackcraft.entry.storage_link: Joins storage without another cable. Every powered Storage Link in a dimension is linked to every other, and all the storage beside them becomes one network: put a link against (or on the fiber of) each Storage Array cluster, and every terminal, Wireless Terminal, Item Pipe and machine reaching any link sees all of it. A machine touching a link (a Site Planner, a Drone Dock, a Launch Control) draws from the whole lot with no pipe at all. Draws 4 kW; it must be powered, which it can be just by touching a powered machine.
guide.rackcraft.entry.storage_terminal: Your window into storage on the same fiber network. Search, take and deposit items; craft on the 3x3 grid, which refills itself from storage; encode Recipe Patterns; and start autocrafting jobs. Ctrl-click a craftable item (marked +) to choose how many to make.
guide.rackcraft.entry.superconducting_py: A Pylon wound with Superconducting Wire. Two of these link up to 256 blocks apart and waste nothing at all. A link to an ordinary Pylon falls back to the ordinary range and loss.
guide.rackcraft.entry.superconducting_wi: Wire with no resistance at all, as long as it stays very cold. Built on the Assembly Line once Advanced Materials is researched: a Cryo Coil wound with eight Copper Wire, two Hydrogen Canisters of coolant, then welded and riveted. Used in Cryostats, Quantum Annealers and Exascale Cabinets.
guide.rackcraft.entry.suppression_canist: A pressurised extinguishing agent that is loaded into a Fire Suppression Tank.
guide.rackcraft.entry.survey_satellite: Bus + a Thermal Scanner + 2 Circuit Boards, riveted. One stage. It photographs the world once and drops the results into the Launch Control: a map marking the nearest Hyperscale Campus nobody has found yet (or, failing that, the nearest abandoned data center).
guide.rackcraft.entry.survey_stake: A stick with a flag on it, for telling a Site Planner where to build. Use it on the ground at one corner of the site and then at the opposite corner; while you hold it the site is outlined. Use it on a Site Planner to hand the site over. Sneak-use to start again.
guide.rackcraft.entry.tanker_drone: A big, fast hydrogen hauler, and the one drone you can't build: it is only sold at the Crypto Exchange, for a great deal of RackCoin, and only once Cryogenic Hydrogen Storage is researched. Put it in a Hydrogen Tank's slot and it flies a stack of canisters at a time from the tank to any Drone Dock, Site Planner or Launch Control within 256 blocks whose hydrogen slot isn't full, then comes back for more. Docks on the tank's own pipes already draw from it, so tankers serve the far ones.
guide.rackcraft.entry.tape_cartridge: Cold storage for 1,048,576 items. Goes in a Tape Library. Cheap and huge, but players wait two seconds for each read.
guide.rackcraft.entry.tape_library: Cold storage. Holds four Tape Cartridges of a million items each and draws only 0.3 kW. Items on tape take two seconds to mount before they reach your inventory. When your drives pass 85% full, the items you have not used for longest are archived to tape automatically.
guide.rackcraft.entry.teleport_pad: Stand on it for two seconds and you arrive on the pad it is entangled with, anywhere in the dimension. Entangle two pads by using a Linked Shard on one and then the other (a Dimensional Shard for pads in different dimensions, at twenty times the cost); sneak-use a shard to cut a pair. Each pad needs a Quantum Annealer in its slot and a Cryostat touching it. A jump burns a Hydrogen Canister from the source's Cryostat and a burst of power from its network, a megawatt-second per 100 blocks, so the grid has to be able to answer: the screen shows what a jump costs. The pad you land on only needs its Annealer and a stocked Cryostat. Needs room above both pads. Inert until Quantum Entanglement is researched.
guide.rackcraft.entry.tensor_accelerator: An AI card. It can't mine, but it lends 12 AI compute to contract generation and model training, which pays about a third more than a GPU Blade mining in the same bay. It draws 0.8 to 2.6 kW and needs freshwater cooling (2 units).
guide.rackcraft.entry.terraformer_cannon: Flattens, fills or hollows ground in a radius, instantly. Right-click a block to fire at it. Sneak-use in the air to cycle modes (Flatten, Fill, Hollow, Smooth); use it in the air to cycle the radius from 3 to 16. Every 256 blocks moved burns a Hydrogen Canister. It never touches a Rackcraft machine, a chest or bedrock.
guide.rackcraft.entry.terraforming_drone: A quadcopter with a scoop. Load it into a Site Planner and it levels the site: it digs up to five blocks off the high spots each trip and drops them into the low ones, takes spare earth home to storage, and brings dirt or cobblestone from storage when there is more hole than hill. When the ground is even it docks and waits. Built on the Assembly Line from a Heavy Drone Frame.
guide.rackcraft.entry.text_corpus: Several thousand words a librarian really didn't want to write. Upload it to one of the Gemerald language models (Flash-Lite, Flash, Pro) at an Operations Terminal.
guide.rackcraft.entry.thermal_scanner: Hold it to see coloured heat particles in every warm air cell within 24 blocks: blue is cool and red is past 40 C. Right-click a rack while holding it to read the inlet and exhaust temperatures.
guide.rackcraft.entry.tower_frame: A ring of steel for a Wind Tower. A Welding Robot and a Riveting Robot turn it into a Tower Section.
guide.rackcraft.entry.tower_section: One more block of Wind Tower, built on the Assembly Line from a Tower Frame (a weld and some rivets). Stack them straight up and put a Wind Tower Nacelle on top; power runs down the tower to the ground. Thin enough that air passes it.
guide.rackcraft.entry.trunk_bundle: One thick conduit that carries power, coolant and fiber at the same time: three networks in one block, instead of three runs side by side. It joins any power cable, coolant pipe or fiber cable it touches, and machines of those kinds, each on its own lane. A cut trunk cuts all three lanes at once, and one splice from a Repair Kit mends them. Inert until Structured Cabling is researched.
guide.rackcraft.entry.uplink_router: Provides 100 units of bandwidth to its fiber network. A rack needs bandwidth equal to its mining rate in RC/s; with less, earnings are scaled down proportionally.
guide.rackcraft.entry.uranium_mill: Grinds and leaches Raw Uranium into Yellowcake: two ore make one. Like every nuclear machine it is a multiblock: build Uranium Mills into a solid cube, 2x2x2 up to 5x5x5 (or 10x10x10 with research), to make it work at all. Every block in the cube is a core: each core finishes one batch every 30 seconds and draws 20 kW while working, and bigger cubes use up to 20% less power per core. Inputs are shared evenly across the cube; feed and empty it from any block, by hand, hopper or Item Pipe.
guide.rackcraft.entry.uranium_ore: Faintly glowing ore found deep down, from Y -64 to Y 16, in small veins. Mine it with an iron pickaxe for Raw Uranium (Fortune helps, Silk Touch keeps the ore). Raw Uranium can't be smelted: it goes to a Uranium Mill, two to a Yellowcake, and a Fuel Cell takes twelve.
guide.rackcraft.entry.utility_intake: A grid connection supplying 100 kW of steady power. It drops to zero during a Utility Outage event, so pair it with batteries and diesel backup.
guide.rackcraft.entry.wafer_fab: A chip fab in a box, or rather in a cube: it etches sixteen Silicon and four GPU Chips into one Wafer-Scale Engine, five minutes per batch per core, 400 kW per working core. It is a multiblock: build a solid cube of 2x2x2 up to 5x5x5 (or 10x10x10 with research) Wafer Fabs. It does nothing until the Extreme UV Lithography research is done at an Operations Terminal, and a 3x3x3 draws over 10 MW while it works, so plan on a reactor array. Feed and empty it from any block, by hand, hopper or Item Pipe.
guide.rackcraft.entry.wafer_scale_engine: The endgame AI module: a whole silicon wafer as one chip. It lends 150 AI compute and 40 general compute (three Quantum Cores' worth of AI) and draws 2 to 16 kW, so a full rack is 128 kW of heat. It can't mine, it is liquid-cooled, and it boots in 20 seconds. It can't be crafted or bought: only a Wafer Fab makes it. Hardware failures never take one out.
guide.rackcraft.entry.waste_cask: Four Spent Fuel rods sealed behind steel and depleted uranium. Completely safe to carry, stack and store: line them up on a concrete pad somewhere and try not to think about the next ten thousand years.
guide.rackcraft.entry.water_heat_exchang: Heat sink for a coolant loop that dumps heat into a body of water: place it touching water and it takes 3 kW per water source block within four blocks, up to 120 kW. Sea water works, and the water is never used up. Draws 0.5 kW.
guide.rackcraft.entry.welding_arm: A robot arm with a plasma torch. Place it beside a Conveyor Belt, facing the belt, and it welds every workpiece that needs welding as it passes: six seconds per weld, drawing 1,500 kW while the torch is lit and 1 kW waiting. Below full power it welds slower, and under 10% it stops. Sparks fly; don't stand in them.
guide.rackcraft.entry.wind_nacelle: The business end of a Wind Tower: a generator with three great blades, built on the Assembly Line. Put it on top of at least ten Tower Sections stacked in a column, facing into open air: the blades need a clear 5x5 in front of it. It makes 120 kW at Y 130, more higher up (up to 150 kW above Y 150), half again in a thunderstorm, and rises and falls with the wind like a turbine. A tall tower on low ground reaches the good wind anywhere. Its power comes down the tower to whatever touches the bottom section. It wears like a Solar Array, so keep a Drone Dock nearby.
guide.rackcraft.entry.wind_turbine: Produces up to 30 kW, depending on altitude and the wind. It runs at 25% at Y 70 or below and reaches full output at Y 130; thunderstorms add another 50%. The wind itself rises and falls by up to a quarter over a few minutes, the same for every turbine, so a battery smooths a wind farm nicely. It needs no fuel and no upkeep. For far more, build a Wind Tower.
guide.rackcraft.entry.wireless_terminal: A Storage Terminal in your pocket. Sneak-right-click a Wireless Transmitter to link it, then right-click anywhere in range. Beyond its range or in another dimension it needs an upgraded transmitter.
guide.rackcraft.entry.wireless_transmitt: Lets a Wireless Terminal reach this fiber network. Range starts at 16 blocks. Upgrade it in its screen with RackCoin or with resources: up to 1,024 blocks, then unlimited in this dimension, then every dimension. Each level doubles its power draw.
guide.rackcraft.entry.writing_desk: Training data for the language model. Use Shackles on a librarian within six blocks to chain them to the desk, then stock it with paper and ink sacs. The librarian writes a Librarian Text Corpus every 30 seconds from two paper; an ink sac lasts four. Connect it to a Storage Array with Item Pipe and it restocks itself and files the corpora in storage. They can't leave and complain about it constantly. Sneak-right-click them with an empty hand to set them free.
guide.rackcraft.entry.yellowcake: Uranium oxide concentrate from a Uranium Mill. Six of it go into a Gas Centrifuge for one Enriched Uranium.
guide.rackcraft.fuel_notes: Each tick of furnace burn time gives one tick of 40 kW, and fuel only burns while the generator is supplying power. Coal runs 80 s, a coal block 800 s and a lava bucket 1000 s (the bucket stays in the slot).
guide.rackcraft.line_next: The assembly line continues on the next page.
guide.rackcraft.no_recipe: No recipe. Found in the world or produced by machines.
guide.rackcraft.recipes_next: Recipes continue on the next page.
guide.rackcraft.title: Rackcraft Field Manual
rack_status.rackcraft.booting.hint: Racks start slowly once they have power: a couple of seconds per Pi Node, four per 1U Server, five per ASIC, eight per GPU Blade or Tensor Accelerator and fifteen per Quantum Core, so a full rack of Quantum Cores takes two minutes. Power, mining and heat ramp up as it boots. Losing power means booting from cold again.
rack_status.rackcraft.crafting.hint: This rack is lending its compute to an autocrafting job, so it is not mining. It resumes when the job finishes.
rack_status.rackcraft.empty.hint: Put Pi Nodes, 1U Servers, ASIC Miners, GPU Blades, Tensor Accelerators or Quantum Cores into the eight bays on the left. Each module takes one bay.
rack_status.rackcraft.generating.hint: This rack is generating work for an AI contract, which pays better than mining. It goes back to mining when the item is finished.
rack_status.rackcraft.leased.hint: This rack is serving a Compute Lease. Keep it powered and cool: the client only pays in full if the lease's uptime guarantee is met.
rack_status.rackcraft.mining.hint: Everything is working. RackCoin goes to the shared balance; spend it at a Crypto Exchange.
rack_status.rackcraft.needs_cdu: Stopped: Quantum Core needs a CDU
rack_status.rackcraft.needs_cdu.hint: Place a Coolant Distribution Unit directly beside this rack.
rack_status.rackcraft.needs_cryostat: Stopped: Quantum Annealer needs a Cryostat
rack_status.rackcraft.needs_cryostat.hin: Place a Cryostat directly beside this rack, give it power and load it with Hydrogen Canisters (an Item Pipe to storage or a Hydrogen Tank keeps it topped up). Each running Annealer boils off a canister every 5 minutes.
rack_status.rackcraft.needs_water.hint: ASIC Miners, GPU Blades, Tensor Accelerators and Quantum Cores are liquid-cooled. Run Coolant Pipe from this rack to a heat sink: a Cooling Tower, Dry Cooler, Chiller or Water Heat Exchanger. The pipe carries 85% of their heat away.
rack_status.rackcraft.network_limited.hi: The routers on this fiber network can't carry every rack. Add another Uplink Router or a Core Router.
rack_status.rackcraft.no_miners.hint: Its modules (Tensor Accelerators, NPUs, Neuromorphic Cores, crafting hardware and the like) can't mine. They earn by lending compute: keep its cluster on Auto and give it AI contracts, leases, training, research or autocrafting at the Operations Terminal. Add miners if you want it earning RackCoin between jobs.
rack_status.rackcraft.no_network.hint: Run Fiber Cable from this rack to an Uplink Router so it can mine.
rack_status.rackcraft.no_power.hint: Connect this rack to a generator, solar panel or utility intake with Power Cable.
rack_status.rackcraft.overheated.hint: The intake air is 40 C or hotter. Heat that doesn't go into a coolant loop goes into the room: catch it with a Rear-Door Cooler on the rack's back, take it out of the air with a CRAC unit or exhaust fan, and keep hot exhaust away from intakes. If To loop is less than the rack's heat, its loop is overloaded: add sinks.
rack_status.rackcraft.researching.hint: This rack is working on a research project or a frontier training run from the Operations Terminal's R&D tab, so it is not mining. Set its cluster to Mining at the terminal to keep it mining instead.
rack_status.rackcraft.throttled.hint: The intake is above 27 C, so the rack slows down. Check where its heat goes (To loop / To air): put a Rear-Door Cooler or CDU on its back (either catches the exhaust into the loop), add sinks to its coolant loop, or pull hot air away with a CRAC unit or exhaust fan. A solid block behind a rack pushes its exhaust out sideways, often straight into the next aisle.
rack_status.rackcraft.training.hint: This rack is training an AI model on uploaded data. Set its cluster to Mining at an Operations Terminal to keep it mining instead.
rack_status.rackcraft.tripped.hint: Power dropped below 50%. The rack restarts once power is back and the intake is under 32 C.
screen.rackcraft.suppression_hint: Load a Suppression Canister into the slot above.
storage.rackcraft.no_pattern: No Recipe Pattern for %s is stored on this network
storage.rackcraft.not_linked: Sneak-right-click a Wireless Transmitter to link this terminal
storage.rackcraft.offline: No storage reachable: check power, fiber and that the arrays are not overheated
storage.rackcraft.other_dimension: The transmitter is in another dimension; it needs the multidimensional upgrade
storage.rackcraft.out_of_range: Out of range: %s blocks away, transmitter reaches %s
storage.rackcraft.status.asleep.hint: The storage network's area isn't loaded, so the job is paused until it is.
storage.rackcraft.status.bad_pattern.hin: A pattern no longer matches any recipe. Encode it again.
storage.rackcraft.status.crafting.hint: Server racks on this fiber network are lending compute. Each point of compute makes 0.25 crafts per second.
storage.rackcraft.status.no_compute.hint: No rack can lend compute: there are no working racks on this storage's fiber network, and no online cluster (racks with an uplink router) set to Auto is free. ASIC Miners can't craft.
storage.rackcraft.status.offline.hint: Storage is offline: check power, fiber and that the arrays are not overheated.
storage.rackcraft.status.queued.hint: Starts on the next simulation step.
storage.rackcraft.status.waiting.hint: An ingredient ran out mid-job, probably taken out of storage. Put more in and the job carries on.
storage.rackcraft.transmitter_offline: The linked transmitter is unpowered or gone
tooltip.rackcraft.drive: Hot storage: goes in a Storage Array
tooltip.rackcraft.multimeter: Right-click a machine or cable to measure; sneak-right-click a machine to rotate
tooltip.rackcraft.tape: Cold storage: goes in a Tape Library, 2 s to read
transmitter.rackcraft.link_hint: Sneak-right-click this block with a Wireless Terminal to link it.
